summary: Open-source context database that stores an AI agent's knowledge, memory and skills as a browsable virtual filesystem.

heroCommands.comment: Install and set up the server
heroCommands.command: uv tool install openviking --upgrade && openviking-server init

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenViking is a context database for AI agents. Instead of hiding memory inside embeddings, it organises everything an agent knows (knowledge, memory and skills) as a virtual filesystem under viking:// that both agents and people can browse.
sixtySeconds.problem: Most agent memory is a black box: text goes in, embeddings come out, and nobody can see what was stored. OpenViking makes agent context visible and organised in one place.
whoFor: Developers building AI agents with long-term memory
Builders of RAG systems who want inspectable storage
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to unify agent memory, RAG knowledge and skills in one transparent store, self-hosted or as a hosted service.
requirements: A model provider with an embedding model and a chat model

overview: You can try OpenViking Studio in the browser with no install, or self-host the server. The setup wizard (openviking-server init) writes ~/.openviking/ov.conf and supports Volcengine, OpenAI, Codex OAuth, Kimi, GLM and local Ollama.
You can also let your coding agent deploy it by pointing it at the setup-for-agent guide in the docs; it asks for your model provider and keys first.
Hosted versions are run by Volcengine and BytePlus; the README says the first 50 files are free on the Volcengine service. The project is AGPL-3.0 licensed.
